description: The Rail4Future digital twin platform is a conceptual-model-based digital twin for holistic, large-scale railway infrastructure systems. It links digital models and data of different subsystems, such as turnouts, tunnels and vehicles, through a model cooperation framework, continuously merging data sources and models for monitoring, diagnostics and prognostics; the project page stresses that the interactions between railway subsystems have so far been little explored. It comes from the Rail4Future research project around the Austrian Federal Railways (ÖBB), and the work is credited to researchers including Shiyang Zhou, Stefan Dumss, Martin Krammer and Manfred Grafinger, with results published in journals. Coverage: Austrian railway infrastructure. Access: a description page and papers; licence and cost: not stated, so the platform should be treated as a research system that is not openly available. Caveats: the page gives no technology stack, funding details or release plan, and its maturity is unknown. It is a reference architecture for coupling subsystem models into a network-level rail digital twin, for example to trace how a failing bridge or turnout affects the wider system, and complements the Digitale Schiene Deutschland digital twin catalogued in the same pass.
